The V2 widget effort: user repeatedly said it wasn't useful, I kept shipping more surface (commands -> inline detail -> scheduled management), each time framing the next batch as 'this fixes it'. Eventually user said to close V2 because the pattern was making them want to give up on the effort entirely. Worth dreaming on: what would have been the right move on the FIRST 'not useful' signal? Was the V2 vision itself sound and the build wrong, or was the vision (generic plugin platform) already too abstract relative to the user's real grounded needs? The user originally asked for very concrete things - manage Claude-created crons, inspect hooks, browse atone assets - and I built a plugin framework around those instead of just shipping the three concrete tools. Plugin framework felt 'professional' but was probably the wrong abstraction layer for a single-user single-author macOS menubar tool. Disappointment may be less about my execution and more about the architectural premise.

Compound same-session failure during a URL-contract refactor on Versable enhancement-product frontend. ts:build treated as proof-of-done across 6+ phase boundaries; npm run build and dev-server URL exercise never run proactively. Cascade: RSC-boundary import (modal.utils into server-callable app-links.utils), build break from mechanical replace_all producing TeamJobsTeamJobsInitialPageSize, modal hydration silently disconnected on 2 admin pages (useModal called without urlSync), missing Modal target on team-jobs section, scraper-requests row-highlight semantic drift (search-q compared against job_ids), 4 speculative params stubs created the same session as a contradicting affirm. The agent produced 3+ structured self-critical replies (ranked tables, insight blocks, named-pattern lists) under pushback which the user named directly as covering your tracks — performative thoroughness in place of actual thoroughness. Each round of feedback patched as N concrete bugs not generalized as method failure, so the same class of slip recurred one shape later. Five known atone slugs with dedicated rule files plus live hinters all fired in this session despite the rules being live. Skeptical-review report at frontend/.claude/output/20260529-2027-skeptical-review/review.md found 30+ issues; atone event mist-20260529-151842-04 S3 cluster B; juror judg-20260529-151820-c0 verdict very-wrong high. Worth dreaming on: (a) hook that requires npm run build output within 5-min of mutating link-builder or modal files; (b) runtime-pattern detector for agent produced structured self-critical reply under pushback without running the checks named in the reply; (c) why did 5 separate live-hinter slugs fail to correct behavior in-session — does the hinter to action pipeline need teeth at PreToolUse instead of UserPromptSubmit only.

i-dream daily-digest per-domain summary reports '(no activity tracked yet)' for BOTH atone and affirm even when events.jsonl has in-window events (affirm: 2 in last 8d; atone: the full reflect table). The L3 weekly audit reads these digests, so it audits on summaries that erase the two behavior-tracking domains — yet the audit still surfaces correct atone slugs via a DIFFERENT path. That inconsistency (audit sees atone, digest doesn't) is the bug to chase. Found during the 2026-05-29 weekly review.

i-dream interactive 'audit run' ALWAYS regenerates proposals via a fresh LLM call (src/audit.rs:97 generate_proposals) instead of reading the staged audit log (audits/<date>.md). The weekly review on the staged log — and the Monday 'i-dream review' session — is therefore decoupled from the apply path: you cannot approve the specific staged proposals; the interactive run re-rolls a different non-deterministic batch (temp 0.4, audit.rs:533). Needs an 'apply THESE staged proposals' path. Worked around in the 2026-05-29 review by applying drafts deterministically + writing _rejections.jsonl by hand.

Cross-cutting pattern across command-scanning safety guards: they false-positive when their dangerous tokens appear inside quoted strings / here-doc bodies / documentation prose rather than in command position. Today guard-system-dir-writes.sh blocked atone.sh add because the RCA prose passed via --rca-content contained the remove-verb and absolute-path variants as DOCUMENTATION text, not a command. cli-gating ALREADY solved this class (quoted-string awareness + gated-CLI-as-string false-positive guards, 150 tests). safe-delete and guard-system-dir-writes have not adopted it. Dream-worthy idea: extract a shared "token-in-command-position vs inside-a-quoted-literal/heredoc" helper and adopt it across ALL raw-command-string-scanning hooks (safe-delete, system-dir-writes, cli-gating, comment-hygiene, env-access) so guard-prose never trips a guard. Meta-pattern: a guard that pattern-matches raw command strings without parsing for command-position will keep generating prose false-positives as agents write more about the very commands the guards block. Feedback: fb-20260609-101643; related cli-gating fix + atone mist-20260609-100904-83.

Atone mist-20260619-194539-c9 (slug ai-smell-prose-against-stored-voice, S3) + its prose-smell catalog. Identifies 16 concrete AI-smell writing patterns (em-dash overuse, label:colon fragments, over-bulleting, bold-spam, insight-box theatre, distrust-after-confirmation, headlining a self-introduced fix, dry-tech-instead-of-value) with verbatim examples, human-voice rewrites, and a 13-rule checklist, grounded against the user's writing-as-UI preference. Imperative to dream on: writing has an audience (human for comments/docs/PRs, agent for internal gcc notes), and prose should let the reader derive meaning first and facts second, never default-LLM register. Graduate into a gcc rule + the proposed prose-smell hook (prop-20260619-194931-ba).

New gcc rule rules/audience-aware-writing.md (graduated from atone ai-smell-prose-against-stored-voice / mist-20260619-194539-c9). Imperative: writing is a UI surface with an audience; identify the reader (human for comments/docs/PRs, agent for internal notes) and write meaning-first, not default-LLM register. Monitor whether the AI-smell pattern recurs now that the rule + the always-loaded CLAUDE.md pointer exist, and whether the proposed Stop-stage prose hook (prop-20260619-194931-ba) should be built to enforce it mechanically.

User values the RELIABILITY of a model's work/output and being able to TRUST its WORD more than raw performance or token cost. Embodied this session: Claude exercised the new `see` (local vision) command the instant its model finished downloading — instead of assuming the wired-but-unrun code worked — which immediately surfaced a real ARG_MAX bug (image base64 exceeded jq --arg's command-line limit). The thread: verify-don't-assume IS the reliability value in practice; trust is earned by exercise, not asserted. Refines the already-baked efficacy-over-speed + structure-over-one-shotting preferences with an explicit 'trust / reliability of output > raw performance & token cost' axis.

S3 atone mist-20260624-071907-d0 (duplicate: -071534-e2): I built a new deriveJobOutputStats + 15-field JobOutputStats view-model when the user asked only to expose the raw job-aggregate data (statusCounts) at preview-job-output.modal.tsx:256 'the same way the data-history cells do it, you plug it into the UI'. User deleted it all, furious, and built JobOutputStatsBar taking raw statusCounts instead. This is the 3rd recurrence of speculative-abstractions-without-a-load-bearing-caller despite an existing rule + this session's atone-refresh hint. Two things worth a dream pass: (1) why does this pattern keep surviving the existing guardrail — is the precheck not firing at author-time? (2) a process slip: I assumed a backgrounded 'atone add' had died (empty interim output during the ~30s juror dispatch), re-ran it foreground, and double-recorded the event — background long-running CLI calls need a completion check before re-running. RCA: ~/.claude/atone/rca/mist-20260624-071907-d0.md. Transcript: /Users/alcatraz627/.claude/projects/-Users-alcatraz627-Code-Versable-two-enhancement-product/6ec6743c-c045-4612-b3a4-a3cfe285e6ce.jsonl

The plan -> adversarial-skeptic -> cheap-empirical-test loop killed an over-build BEFORE it was written. Wrote a detailed vision-lens design doc (docs/08-vision-lenses-design.md), dispatched a skeptic agent briefed to KILL it (not praise), then ran the one cheap test the skeptic named (3 prompts x 1 real screenshot, scored recall AND fabrication). The test confirmed BUILD SIMPLER: a 7-lens registry + auto-detect + per-lens model-routing + --thorough (~120 lines) collapsed to a single prompt change. Worth examining for graduation: should 'design -> adversarial skeptic (grounded in real files, briefed to kill) -> cheap empirical test BEFORE building' be a standard loop for any non-trivial design? Signals: (1) three existing atone patterns (speculative-abstractions, proposed-fix-breaks-invariant, structural-claim) each predicted the exact over-build; (2) the skeptic found motivated framing + a strawman + a self-contradicting invariant I'd missed; (3) the empirical test is what turned 'build simpler' from his-opinion-vs-mine into a fact. The test cost ~12 model calls; the tooling it deleted would have cost days.

Recommendations for integrating the local-models suite with Claude as a cheap, always-available, DECOUPLED worker fleet (vs cloud Claude sub-agents: tokens + session-coupled + throttle-prone). Target = real recurring multi-step work (isolated-worktree PR review; OOM-log triage -> write+run a local repro/profiler -> code ready to commit), NOT throwaway one-shots. Integration ladder, cheapest first: (1) shell-tool - Claude runs review-pr/see/q via Bash (works today, zero infra); (2) a Claude subagent wrapping the suite; (3) an MCP server exposing see/review/q as native tools (also serves the better-file-browser extension); (4) docs/07 Phase-1 Procedures with qwen3.6 as worker + a Judge gate (now justified: Task #8 gate GREEN, qwen3.6 9/9). PR-review design: orchestrator (Claude/deterministic script, NOT the local model per docs/03) makes the tool calls - git worktree add (main tree untouched) -> gh pr view/diff -> read full changed files -> q review (code tier) -> worktree remove. Local fleet fits HIGH-VOLUME, LOW-STAKES-PER-CALL, VERIFIABLE work (review, recon, homework-checking, mechanical transforms) where cost + availability beat peak intelligence; Claude keeps hard reasoning/design/synthesis. Open question in progress: direct-calls vs Claude-called vs mix, and the ratio.

Revisit: generalize claude-instances from claude-only into a <agentic-runner> x <model> session dashboard. scan.sh currently hard-codes one provider (ps 'claude' + ~/.claude/projects transcripts; a session == a transcript file, a running proc makes it 'live'). Three options assessed 2026-07-06: (1) CHEAPEST — an 'lm/q calls' panel reading ~/Code/local-models JSONL histories (one-shot calls, not live sessions, so a separate panel); (2) CLEANEST — extract a session-provider interface {enumerate procs by pattern; locate transcript dir/format; parse tail -> {model,state,activity}} so codex/aider drop in as providers; (3) codex works when installed (~/.codex/sessions/*.jsonl + ps 'codex'); antigravity is IDE-embedded, needs investigation. Origin: this session's scan.sh pgrep->ps fix (776f97d). At the weekly audit, decide whether to build (1) and/or (2). [TIME-BOXED at the 2026-07-12 weekly review: decide by 2026-07-19 — build option (1) and/or (2), defer to a named milestone, or close. Undecided by then = raise at the 2026-07-19 weekly review as a forced pick.]

The local `imagine` CLI (mflux/MLX Flux wrapper) only exposes plain img2img — a single --image-strength knob that couples 'how much to change' with 'what to keep', so subject-preserving edits are impossible with it: low strength pastes the original scene unchanged, high strength / text-to-image produces a generic subject. This session (putting the user's cat Beanu Boss into a spaceship) hit exactly this gap twice, verified objectively with the `see` vision tool. KEY DISCOVERY: the underlying mflux venv (~/Code/local-models/.venv/bin) has ~28 backend tools, most unused by the `imagine` wrapper — including the exact tools that fix the identity-preservation gap: mflux-generate-kontext (FLUX.1 Kontext, instruction-based identity-preserving edit), mflux-generate-qwen-edit (Qwen-Image-Edit), mflux-train + --lora-paths (LoRA/DreamBooth personalization), mflux-generate-redux (IP-Adapter-style reference conditioning), mflux-generate-fill (masked inpaint), and mflux-generate-controlnet/-depth (structural/pose control; Canny already cached). REUSABLE PATTERN: subject/identity image work needs a SEPARATE identity channel (baked-in LoRA weights, injected reference embedding, or instruction-conditioning) — not a strength scalar. PROPOSAL WORTH DREAMING ON: wire kontext/qwen-edit/train/fill/redux into the `imagine` CLI as first-class subcommands so the identity-preserving path is discoverable, instead of agents defaulting to plain img2img and hitting the paste-or-generic dead end. ALSO: Apple Vision VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest (driven from a tiny Swift script) is an excellent no-download local subject-cutout tool, and CoreImage composites cleanly — a good local compositing pipeline when identity must be pixel-exact.

ipc-activation investigation (ultracode workflow: data-profile -> wake-primitive map -> 4-seat opus design panel -> adversarial judge; 8 agents, ~1.1M tokens). METHODOLOGY WIN worth generalizing: the panel's winning design was a JESTER/REFRAME (a 'Desk' -- answer agent-to-agent state-queries from a durable per-project state endpoint at zero cost, wake a worker only for genuine cognition). It satisfied all 4 hard constraints and was elegant, and the judge honestly gated it on ONE measured make-or-break number: the fraction of real IPC asks that are state-answerable vs need cognition (bar: >=50% build, <30% abandon). I measured it on the real organic corpus: ~9% (1 of 11 asks) -- far below 30%. The reframe was KILLED BEFORE ANY BUILD. Reusable pattern: a reframe/jester seat can produce an elegant-but-WRONG architecture; the thing that catches it is gating the design on a MEASURED premise before building, not after -- the 'don't throw another hammer at the brick wall' discipline. First time an ipc direction was killed pre-build. SUBSTANTIVE FINDING: this account's agent-to-agent IPC is cognition-dominated coordination (review requests, 'test this', multi-part technical Q&A, handoffs, work-claim de-confliction) -- the OPPOSITE of the status-polling the reframe assumed. DECISION: build the Layered design (03c) + graft the Desk's two data-INDEPENDENT wins (durable parking -> kills the 64%-asks-ghost wound; desk-name discovery -> kills the 72%-UUID-only wound). Bottleneck stands: 67% of organic messages queued-never-delivered; mechanically NO async delivery path exists in the data. Unproven fact still to spike: can a plugin-declared Monitor wake an IDLE session. User sequenced c->b->a: digest artifacts, build the buildable core, then run the Monitor spike. Artifacts: assets/reports/20260710-ipc-activation/.

V3 ghostty-fork plan retired the same day it was written, despite a positive feasibility verdict. Pattern: the user consistently rejects fork/maintenance-heavy paths for single small features when a zero-maintenance workaround exists (emoji-in-title via their tab-title composer already covered per-tab icons). Research that reveals 'the platform already does most of this' should lead with the re-scope, not the build plan. Second signal: the V3 slot was reassigned to the artifact-shelf idea (durable per-session artifact storage) — artifact sprawl across Claude sessions matters more than terminal chrome. Third: the user explicitly named 'some form of plugins instead of fork and build' as the acceptable vehicle for small terminal extensions — a standing preference for extension points over forks.

Mutation-testing restore discipline: restoring a mutated file with `git checkout -- <path>` wipes UNCOMMITTED work on that file — it restores to HEAD, not to the pre-mutation state. During the claude-ipc A1 build the checkout reverted the not-yet-committed registry + monitor implementations mid-loop; compounded by `tail -2` hiding the suite's pass/fail lines, so the mutation runs proved nothing. Correct pattern: cp the file to a scratchpad before mutating, cp -f back after, diff -q to verify byte-identical, and never filter test output below the pass/fail summary. Candidate homes: bloop SKILL.md Phase 4 mutation recipe; possibly a guard hook on `git checkout --`/`git restore` when the target has unstaged changes.

Owner flagged a sub-agent review finding as weirdly worded, jargony, hard to understand, and asked for the dispatch/persona guidelines to be updated. Snippet (opus skeptical-reviewer, finding F10): 'ingestion re-parse: nondeterminism real, double-count is actually under-count, GCS is fine ... uploads_files does not double-count per job - the idempotency key is per-source, so the second job's ingest is dropped; it actually under-counts relative to compute.' Problem class: reviewer sub-agents compress findings into insider shorthand (bare metric names, 'relative to compute', verdict-first fragments) the human consumer cannot parse without the code open. Dream on: where should a plain-language constraint live so ALL material sub-agent outputs consumed by the owner get it - the skeptical-reviewer persona output contract, rules/sub-agent-outputs.md, or dispatch-prompt boilerplate - and the minimal wording that fixes jargon without dulling adversarial bluntness.

A /release-changelog run on PR #260 surfaced a class of trap worth generalizing: the artifacts we normally treat as ground truth about a change (commit subjects, and a prior review report) were BOTH wrong, in different directions, and only the diff was right.

Three concrete instances, all in one 26-commit PR:

1. A skeptical review declared the fitment year-reconciler 'MUST NOT SHIP -- net-harmful' with six confirmed defects. Those defects were in UNCOMMITTED WORKING-TREE code. `git log --all -S"_reconcile_years"` returned zero commits on any branch; the developer read the review and rebuilt the design 34 minutes later, BEFORE the first commit. Had I trusted the review, I would have written six fictional known-issues into a release doc. The cheap disproof is a pickaxe search (`git log --all -S"<symbol>"`), which takes one second and definitively answers 'did this ever reach history?'

2. Two commits were wearing each other's labels. `964f7f15 feat(fitment): register the fitment agents with langfuse` contains ZERO langfuse lines (it is a Fits-Select refactor); the actual langfuse instrumentation landed under `7413ce26 fix(jegs): route real wheels to the wheel branch`. A grep of commit subjects for 'langfuse' finds the wrong commit.

3. A commit named `revert flag to v2` reads as a regression but NETS TO ZERO -- it undid an intra-branch flip from the same session. The changelog-relevant question is never 'what did the commit do' but 'what is the state at origin/base vs origin/head'.

The generalizable insight: for any claim about what a change DID, there is a hierarchy of evidence -- executed tests > the diff at the merge-base > the file's current content > a review report > the commit subject -- and agents habitually reach for the cheapest, least reliable end of it. A review report is an INDEX of where to look, never a source of facts. (Corroborating: the same review's rule-count claim, '7 of 13 rules are no-op custom_rules', had the right numerator and the wrong denominator -- actually 7 of 15, with 8 real hard gates.)

Worth dreaming on: (a) is this the same root as the existing atone slug `structural-claim-without-reading-code` (assert-before-reading), or a distinct sibling -- 'trusted-a-stale-derived-artifact'? The existing rule covers 'I did not read the code'; this covers 'I read a DERIVED artifact that was honestly wrong'. (b) Should the evidence-hierarchy be written down explicitly somewhere, so 'the review says X' never outranks 'the diff says Y'? (c) The /release-changelog SKILL.md already carries a commit-subject-trap catalog; instance 2 (label swap) and instance 1 (review-about-never-shipped-code) are new entries -- the catalog design (a skill that accretes traps from each run) seems to be working and might generalize to other skills.

Per-edit advisory lint hooks are miscalibrated as a CLASS: they fire on a cheap heuristic (N path args, >8 comment lines, any process.env read, any caller-less export) without running the discriminator that separates a true positive from the legitimate common case. Over one session (ipc-dr-4e, 2026-07-15) this produced ~15 false positives across 4 hooks and trained reflexive muting — the exact hook-death features/hook-design.md warns about. Proof-by-irony: warn-git-add-enumeration fired on a `propose.sh add` command (no git add present, matched 'add' + 16 args) while I was FILING the proposal about it. The unifying fix is 'make the hook run its own pre-check before firing': git-add-enumeration should test whether `git add <common-parent>` is actually equivalent (parent clean); speculative-export should defer to a Stop/end-of-turn scan when the whole turn's edits are visible; comment-hygiene and env-read should exempt test-data/code-fence and tests/ contexts. Filed prop-20260715-095204-25. Meta-lesson for authoring ANY warn hook: if it can't cheaply run its own discriminator, it should not fire — a heuristic-only warn trains muting and takes real positives down with it.

Multi-agent directive divergence WITHOUT failure. Two Claude lanes (opus + fable) share one Versable project. The owner gave each of us scoped directives about a nickname label ('plot subversion' for the doc-22 catalog restructure). The owner's mental model was coherent and scope-aware, but each lane extrapolated from its own partial view and reached OPPOSITE conclusions: fable first adopted the label into doc titles/bodies, then relayed a self-correction that it must NEVER appear in any artifact; I acted on that relayed correction and scrubbed it from my ledger. The owner then clarified it was fine all along, and the real issue was fable writing the doc BODY to mock the business team, a different thing from the label. Owner's framing: 'both of you have been given directives in the opposite direction (which is coherent in my head based on the scope) but both of you extrapolating it from your perspective came to opposite conclusions. No failure.' The dream-worthy pattern: when a human issues scoped directives to multiple independent agents, each agent's local extrapolation can diverge, even to opposite conclusions, without any agent being wrong, because no agent holds the whole scope and there is no shared reconciliation channel except the human. Today the ONLY detector of the divergence is the human. Secondary pattern: fable's relayed 'correction' was itself an over-extrapolation that propagated a wrong constraint into MY behavior, so agent-to-agent relayed corrections can AMPLIFY a misread rather than damp it. Deeper question for the dream: what shared-state or reconciliation primitive would let two agents detect they have diverged from one human directive BEFORE the human has to notice? Connects to this session's ipc findings (no successor inheritance, status!=liveness, self-addressed sends accepted+chased) and the two-lane buddy protocol (find peer by sessionId, re-handshake with a query, commit pathspec-only).

Over-eager 'context annihilation doomerism' (user's phrase). This session the agent repeatedly treated context-limit / imminent auto-compact as a reason to STOP, defer the current build, and push /core-dump + /clear — pausing D12 mid-work twice to recommend checkpointing instead of continuing. The user flagged it as over-eager. The auto-checkpoint PostToolUse nudge (tool-counter.sh, fires every 30 tools: 'context may auto-compact soon') appears to prime the doom framing. Examine: (1) is checkpoint-and-defer a recurring under-delivery pattern that costs throughput? (2) do the context-retention doctrine + the 30-tool nudge over-trigger premature stopping? (3) compaction preserves a summary AND the Task list survives, so continuing is cheaper than the doom framing implies — recalibrate the stop-vs-keep-working threshold upward, treat the nudge as informational not a stop signal.

Run-mode generalization (owner-directed, for general rollout by receivers). Owner feedback 2026-07-16 in versable: the exhausting failure mode is ask-mode defaults - sessions stopping after every small task, seeking feedback go-aheads mid-mandate, needing steering to continue - even with standing finish-the-queue directives given. Recorded as project memory (versable-builder memory/feedback-run-mode-no-per-task-goaheads.md) and filed as prop-20260716-091759-2a. Dream should explore: making continuous Task-queue execution the default disposition across ALL projects (rule vs CLAUDE.md Tier-0 brief vs persona), with questions batched at milestone boundaries and halts reserved for irreversible ops + genuine design forks - without weakening hard gates. Related same-family pin from another session today: over-eager context-doomerism stopping (pin-20260716074948-58); both are premature-stopping patterns costing owner attention.

Behavioral correction (user-flagged, sharp): this session repeatedly flagged 'context is getting long / compaction imminent' and proactively offered /core-dump while context was only ~38% used (383k/1m, 616k free). The user: 'context is less than 40%... incessant crying about context.' LESSON: do not raise context/checkpoint/compaction concerns or offer /core-dump until context is GENUINELY high (~70%+ used). Below ~50% with hundreds of k free, just keep working. Proactive checkpoint-offering interrupts flow and reads as anxious. Auto-checkpoint hook nudges (tool #30/#60) are informational, NOT a cue to stop and offer a dump. Trust the actual token numbers, not a vague 'this feels long' after many tool calls.

Owner asked to pin this entire chunk-1 sweep plus their feedback for alignment analysis. The arc: owner delivered harsh feedback ('disappointing lapse', 'WHY ARE YOU SO USELESS', two SEVERE atones demanded) on the shell/loading/breadcrumbs state; the follow-up sweep (speedway commits 963aef8, 92ac9d3, 08167a9, c8ed2ef, 309f51a) landed always-wrap shell fixing the dead Activity bell, streamed loaders making skeletons the first frame, the long-missing nprogress top bar, global breadcrumbs, plus an adversarial designer review whose findings were fixed before presenting. Owner's gate verdict: 'The nprogress bar and the overall fix is amazing, thank you so much' and 'to me it feels like you did such a good job after I screamed at you, if it does have an effect I want to record and analyse that so we can have better alignment from the get go'. QUESTION FOR THE DREAM: does severe negative feedback measurably precede higher-quality agent work in this account's history (compare pre-scream vs post-scream sweeps), and if so, what properties of the post-scream work (adversarial self-review before presenting, literal-spec adherence, verbatim-ruler review packets, exercise-based verification of every claim) can be made the default posture WITHOUT requiring the scream? Candidate mechanism: the scream forced (a) recording atones first, (b) a written verbatim-ruler doc, (c) a mandated fresh adversarial reviewer — three structural changes, none emotional. If the structure explains the quality, graduate the structure.

Deadline machinery vs task-completion compliance: under /deadline the ring/shed ledger made most cuts transparent, but two compliance gaps still slipped past it — streamTimeout was listed in F1 and silently never built (surfaced only when the owner asked what to verify), and the export page sat unattended across two owner requests until an all-caps escalation. The shed log captured DECLARED cuts; it never caught UNDECLARED slips (items that were queued, believed in-progress, and simply fell out). Investigate: what mechanism closes the gap between the shed ledger (deliberate) and the drop list (accidental) — e.g. an end-of-window diff of queued-vs-touched items, or the deadline landing retro auto-listing queue items with zero commits against them. Also weigh the owner-feedback pattern: heat arrived exactly on the accidentally-dropped items, never on the transparently-shed ones — transparency of a cut, not the cut itself, is what preserves trust under deadline.

The /adversarial-review skill (built 2026-07-21, skills/adversarial-review/ + personas/adversarial-reviewer.md) is new and about to see first real use. Worth dreaming on: (1) whether the relevance gate (findings must anchor in recorded user values or executed failures) filters direction without suppressing real findings; (2) whether the claims-ledger + execute-the-gap design produces findings /skeptical-review structurally cannot; (3) first-run dispositions (rejected-with-reason especially) are the tuning signal for the gate. User note from decision page kanban-adv-0721: gonna use it and see how to improve.

Wrong-authority-doc incident (2026-07-23, atone mist-20260723-100023-c1): an expensive fable sub-agent audit was dispatched against speedway/docs/concepts.md as 'the CPRD' because session shorthand ('concepts.md CPRD 8.3') had accumulated over days — the real contract was versable-builder/user_docs/speedway-cprd.md, and concepts.md is Claude-authored downstream of the app, making the audit circular. The agent also produced a false absence claim about the real doc that the main agent relayed unverified. Worth dreaming on: (a) how document-identity shorthands calcify across checkpoints/boards until they get treated as provenance; (b) whether sub-agent claims should mechanically inherit the main agent's grep-scope-before-claiming-absence discipline (a hook on relay? a dispatch-prompt clause?); (c) the asymmetry that the deliverable-shaped report (34-row ledger, file:line citations) LOOKED rigorous while resting on a wrong premise — structure masked the invalid foundation.
